title: Minimum Desks For Sessions

statement.md: $n$ trading sessions run over time intervals $[s_i, e_i)$ with $s_i < e_i$. A desk can host only one session at a time, but a session ending at time $t$ and another starting at time $t$ can share a desk. Print the minimum number of desks needed to host every session.

hints: The answer is the largest number of sessions running at the same moment.
Sort starts and ends separately and sweep. At equal times, process ends before starts.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "Sort all start times and all end times separately. Sweep with two pointers: if the next start is before the next end, a desk is opened (count up and track the maximum), otherwise a session finished (count down). An end at the same time as a start is handled first, because those two sessions may share a desk. A min-heap of end times gives the same answer. Time $O(n \\log n)$."}]

solutions.python:
import sys


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(tok[0])
    starts = sorted(int(tok[1 + 2 * i]) for i in range(n))
    ends = sorted(int(tok[2 + 2 * i]) for i in range(n))
    j = cur = best = 0
    for s in starts:
        while ends[j] <= s:
            j += 1
            cur -= 1
        cur += 1
        best = max(best, cur)
    print(best)


main()
